newsitem.title: USA: Sega says Saturn sales top 1.2 mln in U.S..
newsitem.headline: Sega says Saturn sales top 1.2 mln in U.S..

text.p: Sega of America, the U.S. unit of video game giant Sega Enterprises Ltd, on Monday said 1996 consumer sales of its Sega Saturn game player topped 1.2 million units in 1996, beating company forecasts.

"Strong (game) titles and good value drove sales beyond our expectations this year, especially during the holidays," Shoichiro Irimajiri, Sega of America's chief executive officer, said in a statement.
The company said the 1.2 million consumer sales caused its installed customer base of Saturn machines in the United States to rise to a total 1.6 million.
The company said it expects the installed base to reach 1.7 million users in the U.S. by the end of March.

Sega sold 400,000 Saturns in 1995 after an initial product launch in September that year. In mid-summer, 1996, Sega cut the price on Saturn to $199.00 in the face of competition from rivals Sony Corp and Nintendo Co Ltd.
Worldwide, the installed base now stands at over 7.0 million units, the company said.

Sales of games for Saturn jumped to 5.5 million in 1996, a 175 percent increase from year ago figures. Sega said its "three pack" promotion contributed some 500,000 unit sales during December. It plans to continue that promotion, which gives Saturn buyers three free games, unti March 31.
Strong titles for the holiday season included "Sonic 3D Blast" and "NiGHTS", Sega said.

Finally a Sega spokesman said the company sold 10,000 units of its NetLink product, which when used with Saturn can connect a television set to the Internet. He said the sales were "a little under" forecasts, but added the company expects the market for these new products to take time to develop.
